page: Microsoft Azure E48as_v6 is an Eav6-family virtual machine powered by a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V74 processor. It features 48 vCPUs mapped to 24 physical cores with multithreading enabled, operating at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz. The system architecture is x86_64, supported by 384.0 GB of RAM, which provides a memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. There is no local storage bundled with this instance, though it is Premium Storage capable, and it includes zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses and no GPU hardware.

Benchmark data indicates strong computational capabilities, with stress-ng single-core and multi-core CPU metrics placing in the top 25%. Memory performance is variable; while cached read-only small-block memory bandwidth is strong at 3648.82 GB/sec, uncached large-block read and write bandwidths drop to average levels of 113.13 GB/sec and 83.12 GB/sec respectively. Cryptographic and integer operations perform well, as evidenced by strong Passmark CPU encryption and database operations scores. However, large-scale language model execution reveals a clear bottleneck, with text generation on a 70B model falling into the bottom 25% at 2.58 tokens/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E48as_v6 offers a dense memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it appropriate for memory-intensive workloads without the overhead of dedicated GPU hardware. The instance is configured for database operations, multi-threaded decompression tasks, and software compilation, as supported by its high Passmark database score and strong Geekbench compiling metrics. It is also appropriate for small-model LLM inference, though larger models require alternative hardware configurations due to memory bandwidth and processing limitations.
